reason: Narrower. In equitant and sheathing monocot leaves (Xyris, Eriocaulaceae and similar), the 'vaginant lamina' is the sheathing lower part of the leaf ('vaginant laminae 1/2 leaf length'). 'Equal/unequal' is a set quality (FLOPO:0991101/0991102) of this sheath.

label: laesura
parent: is_a PO_0009011 (plant structure); part_of PO_0025017 (plant spore)
definition: A plant structure (PO:0009011) that is the scar, straight or Y-shaped (trilete), on the proximal face of a plant spore (PO:0025017), marking where it touched the other spores of its tetrad.
reason: A real spore structure that fern and lycophyte floras use, with no PO class (PO has no parts of the spore wall). Propose to PO upstream as a low-priority request.
The reference measure in a ratio ('strobilus 1/4–1/10 total length'). This is pattern 10 (ratio to another part), whose second term is the whole plant or shoot, not a structure called 'total length'.

target: plant cell (PO_0009002) part_of leaf base (PO_0020040); PO lists 'phyllid base' as a synonym of leaf base
reason: Moss descriptions (brick-red, oval, linear, papillose basal cells of the phyllid). A cell type located in a region of an existing class, so the part-of pattern covers it. 'Inner' and 'toward margin' are positions within that region.
A distribution quality ('scattered oil cells', 'scattered hair scars'). The parts it qualifies are the bearers.
Narrower: ovules of the female flower ('1 ovule par loge', 'uniovulées'). 'Female' qualifies the flower, so it goes through pattern 12 (part of a qualified whole), not a new class.

target: trichome (PO_0000282) part_of fruit (PO_0009001), on the inner fruit wall
reason: In Ceiba and other Bombacoideae, kapok is the mass of hairs from the inner wall of the capsule. These are not seed hairs (PO:0004511 seed trichome would be wrong), so: hairs as part of the fruit, with 'abundant' as an amount.
'Parties herbacées' means all the non-woody parts together (young stems, petioles, leaves, inflorescences). There is no single bearer, and choosing one would be a guess.
Exact: a misspelling or lemmatisation of French 'collétères'. The class exists already.

Narrower: leaves of axillary shoots or fascicles, with position handled by pattern 04 (state or position of the bearer). The small size (1.5 mm wide) suggests reduced leaves of short shoots; still a leaf.
Narrower: in Ficus, the bracts closing the opening (ostiole) of the syconium, which is an inflorescence. FLOPO has no syconium class (only an evidence row), so it maps to inflorescence bract.
An adjective form of callus ('horny callous at tip', 'pli calleux'). As in the previous review (callus: rejected), it is a generic thickening that needs the organ it belongs to.

label: megasporocarp
parent: is_a PO_0009011 (plant structure); part_of PO_0009025 (vascular leaf)
definition: A plant structure (PO:0009011) of a heterosporous water fern (Salviniaceae) that is a hard or membranous closed case derived from the indusium, enclosing a sorus with a single megasporangium (PO:0025201).
reason: PO has neither sporocarp nor megasporocarp. Floras of Azolla and Salvinia count and measure them. Propose to PO upstream together with a general 'sporocarp' (which also covers Marsilea), with megasporocarp and microsporocarp as its kinds.

Narrower: an ant-inhabited domatium, here a hollow stem internode. However, the current definition of FLOPO_0986021 restricts it to leaves and mites; it should be widened to any plant cavity inhabited by arthropods before this rule is used. The internode (PO_0020142) can be kept as a part-of context.
Exact: a hyphenated spelling of an existing class. (PO's 'pseudobulb' synonym of corm PO_0025355 should not be used; see the note on FLOPO_0986027.)

Ambiguous: it can mean pinnae or pinnules of a compound leaf ('6–15 paires de divisions secondaires'), secondary inflorescence branches, or veins ('the secondary ones mostly 3-5'). The organ must come from the context.
Exact synonym of pseudopetiole. Mapped to the class proposed for 'pseudo-petiole' below, as was done earlier for stone → pyrene.

target: plant organ base (FLOPO_0985024) of orchid labellum (FLOPO_0980978); the presence of a claw = clawed (FLOPO:0991169) on the labellum
reason: The claw is the narrowed, stalk-like base of the labellum: a region of an existing class. Shape and width ('linear', 'canaliculate', '4–4.5 mm wide') go on that base region.
Mixed senses: loops of secondary veins ('arches de nervures secondaires') and concentric ornamentation arcs on seeds or spores. Generic; it needs its organ.
Ambiguous: a spore outer layer (perine) with spine cells, a fruit or seed envelope, or the 'inner envelope' of a flower. Generic; it needs its organ.
Generic part ('basal swelling', a perforated swelling, a papillate swelling) on several different organs. Needs the organ it belongs to.

Narrower: dichasium is a synonym of cyme inflorescence, and 'compound' is a kind of it. 'Flowers in compound dichasia' = the inflorescence is present. PO also lists dichasium under thyrse and cincinnus classes; cyme inflorescence is the right general class.
Narrower: a bract in a lateral position, with the position handled by pattern 04. Count and length go on the bract.
A position adjective ('subepidermal bundles present'). The bearer is the bundle.
An adjective qualifying the counted veins or ribs ('8-12 strong pairs of secondary veins').
Generic part ('3 transverse pads', 'a single pad'). Needs the organ it belongs to.
An adverb modifying a shape ('pairs of narrowly elliptic leaflets'). The counted part is the noun that follows it.

label: pseudopetiole
parent: is_a PO_0025001 (cardinal organ part); part_of PO_0025034 (leaf)
definition: A cardinal organ part (PO:0025001) of a leaf (PO:0025034) that is a narrowed, stalk-like portion between the leaf sheath (PO:0020104) or base and the leaf lamina (PO:0020039), resembling a petiole (PO:0020038) but formed from the lamina or sheath, as in many bamboos, Marantaceae, Musaceae and Zingiberales.
reason: A real structure that floras measure and record as present. It is not a petiole (PO_0020038) and not just the leaf lamina base. Together with 'false petiole' it is used by several floras. Propose to PO upstream.
The plural of stipe, a RELATED synonym of stalk, as in previous rule C264. 'Linear/oblanceolate stipes' fits the orchid pollinarium stipe, which is still a stalk.

A count of rows of ornamentation tubercles on seeds or fruits. PO tubercle (PO_0025352) is the cactus podarium, so mapping to it would be wrong. A row is an arrangement, not a part, and the organ must come from the context.
